references.text: Noah is described as righteous and blameless – the immediate explanation for why he found favor in the Lord's eyes.
Lot finds favor in his master's eyes, just as Noah found favor in the Lord's eyes (the expression מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי is used in both places).
Joseph found favor (חֵן) in Potiphar's eyes, mirroring the same expression used of Noah who found favor in God's eyes.
Moses finds favor in the Lord's eyes (מָצָאתָ חֵן בְּעֵינַי) – one of the most direct parallels to the expression in Gen 6:8.

Noah's faith is highlighted as an example: by faith he built the ark and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith – a New Testament elaboration on what it meant for him to find favor with God.
The angel says to Mary, 'You have found favor with God' – a New Testament parallel to the expression about finding favor (חֵן/χάρις) in God's eyes.
Grace is the basis of Noah's obedience; 6:8 explains why 7:5 is possible.
Confirms that Noah's obedience is the concrete outworking of the grace he found in 6:8.
Asa is a typological parallel to Noah; both find favor by doing what is right in God's eyes.
